name: Indiana
nameStory: Indiana means 'Land of the Indians' - a name chosen by white settlers for a place they were in the middle of clearing of Native people. Within about 25 years of statehood, nearly every Native nation had been forced out of the state that carries their name.
capitalStory: Indianapolis is just 'Indiana' plus the Greek word for city. It was built from nothing in 1821 at the exact center of the state, beside the White River - which then turned out to be far too shallow for boats. A capital planned around a highway that didn't work became a rail and road hub instead, and calls itself the Crossroads of America.

funFacts: The Indianapolis 500 is the largest single-day sporting event in the world.
Indiana limestone built the Empire State Building, the Pentagon, and much of Washington DC.
Nobody agrees where the word 'Hoosier' came from, and the arguments have gone on for 200 years.
Indiana has more interstate highway per square mile than almost any other state.
